speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned presenting with hematuria and right flank pain; to help me narrow down the cause, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms and has there been any trauma or recent heavy lifting?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stone (Nephrolithiasis). The presentation of visible hematuria, right flank pain, and a history of recurrent UTIs in a 42-year-old male with no trauma is highly suggestive of a renal stone. Given the acute nature of the pain and hematuria, I would recommend a NON-CONTRAST CT KIDNEY as the next step for definitive imaging.
